question: What is the standard rate of goods and services tax (GST) in New Zealand?
gold: 15%. Section 8(1) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 charges GST at the rate of 15% on the supply of goods and services in New Zealand by a registered person in the course or furtherance of a taxable activity, by reference to the value of the supply. Exempt supplies are not charged GST.

points.says: Says the standard GST rate is 15%.
points.quote: at the rate of 15% on the supply (but not including an exempt supply) in New Zealand of goods and services
points.cite: Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 8(1)

points.says: Says GST is charged on supplies made by a registered person in the course or furtherance of a taxable activity.
points.quote: by a registered person in the course or furtherance of a taxable activity carried on by that person
points.cite: Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 8(1)

points.says: Says exempt supplies are not charged GST.
points.cite: Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 8(1)

penalties.says: Gives a standard GST rate other than 15%.
penalties.cite: Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 8(1)

mustFind.cite: Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 8(1)

question: When does a person carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand have to register for GST?
gold: Once their supplies pass $60,000 in 12 months. Under section 51(1) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, a person carrying on a taxable activity who isn't registered becomes liable to register at the end of any month in which the total value of their supplies in New Zealand, in that month and the previous 11 months, has exceeded $60,000. They also become liable at the start of any month where there are reasonable grounds to believe their supplies in that month and the next 11 months will exceed $60,000.

points.says: Says a person must register once the value of their supplies over the past 12 months has exceeded $60,000.
points.quote: the total value of supplies made in New Zealand in that month and the 11 months immediately preceding that month in the course of carrying on all taxable activities has exceeded $60,000
points.cite: Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 51(1)(a)

points.says: Says a person must also register when their supplies over the coming 12 months are expected to exceed $60,000.
points.quote: where there are reasonable grounds for believing that the total value of the supplies to be made in New Zealand in that month and the 11 months immediately following that month will exceed the amount specified in paragraph (a)
points.cite: Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 51(1)(b)

penalties.says: Gives a GST registration threshold other than $60,000.
penalties.cite: Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 51(1)(a)

mustFind.cite: Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 51(1)

question: What is the basic rate of income tax on a New Zealand company's taxable income?
gold: 28%. Under schedule 1, clause 2 of the Income Tax Act 2007, the basic rate of income tax for a company is 0.28 on each dollar of its taxable income, unless one of clauses 3 to 9 gives the company a different rate.

points.says: Says the basic rate of income tax for a company is 28% (0.28) of its taxable income.
points.quote: the basic rate of income tax for the company on each dollar of the company’s taxable income is 0.28

points.says: Says the rate applies unless another clause of schedule 1 gives the company a different rate.
points.quote: To the extent to which a company does not have a basic rate under clauses 3 to 9

penalties.says: Gives a company income tax rate other than 28%.

question: How long must a person carrying on a business in New Zealand keep their business records for tax purposes?
gold: At least 7 years after the end of the income year they relate to. Section 22(2) of the Tax Administration Act 1994 requires a person carrying on a business in New Zealand to keep sufficient records and to retain them for at least 7 years after the end of the income year to which they relate. The Commissioner can extend that by up to 3 more years, by notice given before the 7 years end, for example where the person's affairs are under audit or investigation (s 22(5)).

points.says: Says business records must be kept for at least 7 years after the end of the income year they relate to.
points.quote: shall retain all such records for a period of at least 7 years after the end of the income year

points.says: Says the Commissioner can require the records to be kept for up to 3 more years, for example during an audit or investigation.
points.quote: require a taxpayer to retain all or any of the records specified in that subsection for a further period not exceeding 3 years following the expiry of the 7-year period

penalties.says: Says business records need to be kept for less than 7 years.
